discourse.title: For me, from me
discourse.excerpt: However high you may rise in social status, however huge may be your bank account, if your parents are neglected in distress, your life has been a tragic waste.
discourse.theme: No rise in status or wealth compensates for neglecting parents in distress — revering them is the measure of a life.

reflection: Swami is blunt: success that leaves parents neglected in distress is a tragic waste, while even the slightest regard for their comfort delights them. Today, check on one elder in your life — a parent, teacher or elder devotee — and meet one small need before it is asked for. (Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 15, 24 Nov 1972; nearest November discourse — no discourse dated 29 November appears in the corpus)

video.title: How Sathya Sai Taught Me Through the Elders in My Life | Komal Ram

seva_nudge: Offer a ride, a meal or a patient listening ear to an elderly devotee or neighbour today — or help an elder at Sai Prema Nilayam Riverside get to the weekly bhajan.
